## TL;DR

The navigation and palette pass reproduced two user-facing failures and fixed
both. On desktop, opening a task deep link erased its task and tab from the URL
before the drawer closed, so refreshing the page lost the selected task. In the
search palette, a task ID written in the familiar `#1186` form did not match,
even though that is how the interface labels IDs. Deep links now stay in the
route while their drawer is open, and the palette accepts a leading `#` when
matching task IDs. I verified both fixes in an isolated local browser and added
regression coverage.

## Work and rationale

The existing Work view opened a task from `?task=<id>` and applied an optional
`?tab=<id>`, but immediately called `router.replace` to remove those parameters
on desktop. The mobile view already retained them while detail was open. That
desktop special case made the address bar stop representing the current UI:
the drawer showed task 1186 on its Changes tab, while the URL had become just
`/work`. A refresh reconstructed only the board. Since this task asks for
deep links that remain usable after reload, the route needs to describe the
open drawer for the duration of that state.

I removed the eager cleanup from Work view task and new-task opening. The shared
Task drawer now removes `task` and `tab` when it actually closes at either
viewport size. It still preserves unrelated query parameters such as a Work
status filter. This keeps refresh and copy-link behavior aligned with the open
drawer, while preventing a dismissed drawer from returning from stale URL
state. The router's existing selected-tab watcher continues to apply the
requested tab when the route is loaded or updated.

The second issue was in `searchAll`: task IDs were compared directly with the
query. The UI renders them with `#`, so `#1186` could not match the bare stored
ID. I normalized only the task-ID comparison by removing one leading hash.
The original query is still used for title, body, documentation, and settings
search, so the adjustment does not broaden those matches.

The regression tests update the desktop deep-link expectations to keep route
parameters while a drawer is open, cover `?task=new`, ensure additional query
keys survive, and remount the Work view to simulate a document reload with the
same task and Changes tab. Search tests now cover the hash-prefixed ID format.
The shared drawer close behavior was verified through the live app at desktop
width, where closing the deep-linked drawer cleared the route parameters.

## Approaches tried

I first traced the behavior through the Work view, shared Task drawer, router,
and deep-link tests. The route watcher already handled out-of-order task
fetches, and a dedicated tab watcher already applied `?tab=changes`; the
failure came specifically from clearing the route after a successful open.
Keeping the URL in place and making close responsible for cleanup was the
smallest change that addresses refresh without changing how a drawer opened
from a board card or search result behaves.

For browser verification I ran `just serve-noauth 7272` from this worktree. The
computer-use browser bridge was unavailable, and the pre-existing native Chrome
window did not provide a stable isolated tab. I stopped using that window and
used a separate headless Playwright Chromium context against the worktree app.
This kept the verification isolated from unrelated browser state.

I checked the dashboard, every declared navigation destination, the fullscreen
diff routes, the Work task/tab deep link, and browser history navigation. The
deep link was loaded, refreshed, and closed. Search was opened with Ctrl+K at
1280px and from the mobile tab bar at 375px; `#1186` returned the task and
opening the result showed the drawer at both widths. The mobile document width
matched the 375px viewport, so the tested Work screen did not overflow
horizontally.

## Challenges and blockers

The browser bridge reported that its access host was unavailable. The existing
Chrome UI was focused on a different user tab than the intended RepoOS page, so
I stopped sending UI input there and continued with an isolated headless
context. No external account or production service was used for QA.

The route sweep produced one API 401 from `/api/project-environments`. The
route handler explicitly requires a signed-in user, even when the shell is
served with preview overrides. The Deployments page itself rendered; I left
that access policy unchanged because changing authentication on an endpoint
that lists project environments is outside this navigation fix. The commit
diff page also showed its expected “commit not found” state for the deliberately
arbitrary hash used to exercise that route. No JavaScript page errors appeared
in the route and interaction runs.

## Key learnings

For this app, a drawer deep link is state, not just an opening instruction. If
the query is cleared while the drawer remains visible, the URL cannot reproduce
what the user is seeing. Query cleanup belongs to the close transition; keeping
that responsibility in the shared drawer also covers desktop and mobile close
paths consistently.

Searchable identifiers should use the same notation that users see elsewhere
in the interface. The stored task ID remains bare, but accepting the visible
hash-prefixed form avoids forcing users to remember an internal representation.

Verification completed: `bun run build:ui` passed. The focused search and
deep-link run passed 58 tests, including the repository test wrapper's
boot-timing pass. The task's scoped `repoos check` remains the final gate before
handoff.
